rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a referent that never resolves leaves the reader stranded mid-slide. This is the diff's main risk surface (window→session swap). Chunk 2 'Context is King' (lines 7-13): line 9 'Two Claude Code sessions.' establishes the noun fresh in-chunk; line 11 'different session. In the other session,' resolves against the same chunk, not a forward or missing referent. Chunk 3 'You steer the answer by loading context' (line 19): 'One more session.' is an immediate continuation of chunk 2's two-session subject into a third — the compendium's own §1 carve-out list names exactly this shape as NOT a violation ('immediate continuation of the previous slide's subject ("one more window")'), and that example is this very file's PRE-diff text. Swapping the noun the carve-out already blesses does not create a new referent problem. Harm absent. PASS.

Harm: pointing at another file by position stops resolving once deck start position changes. Scanned body lines 1-27 for any callback to another document or another lecture: none present, and the diff touched only inline nouns inside three sentences. N/A, no cross-file callback in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: 'the X you did/saw' pointing at a beat that no longer exists strands the reader. This file is the M1 opener (registry order confirmed: curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md:42, and the maintainer block's own 'Placement: M1 opener, after Connections, before the exercise'), so there is no prior module beat to reference, and body carries no such construction. N/A.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a reveal narrated before its guess kills the demo's payoff mid-delivery. Chunk 2 (lines 7-13): guess prompt at line 11 ('Take a guess before it runs. What does Claude suggest now?') precedes the reveal at line 13 ('Something Finnish: salmon, rye bread, meatballs.'). Reading-order sequence is byte-for-byte unchanged by the window→session diff — only the nouns inside the existing sentences were swapped, the guess/reveal ordering was untouched. PASS.

Harm: a chunk with no self-carrying claim projects as empty air. All 4 non-title chunks carry a complete standalone claim: chunk1 (3-5) states the lecture's premise; chunk2 (7-13) the full demo-plus-reveal; chunk3 (15-21) the steering claim plus a second demo beat; chunk4 (23-27) the loop claim. None reduced in size or content by the diff (edits were in-sentence noun swaps only; check-slide-size.js confirms 4 slides, none oversized, none newly empty). PASS.

Harm: a header the chunk's own content contradicts misleads a skimming reader. Chunk 2 header 'Context is King' vs line 9-13: the chunk delivers exactly that claim (same second question, two different answers, attributed to earlier context). Chunk 4 header 'The loop is what you repeat' vs line 27: 'The fix happens once. The loop is what you repeat' restates the header near-verbatim. Unaffected by the diff (no heading text or claim-bearing sentence changed). PASS.

Harm: a cadence tic reads as authorial clutter; one tic can be the whole slide. Checked all six named sub-patterns across all 4 chunks: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' triple (only lone single negations at line 19 'Not because Claude knows medicine...' and line 27 'Not by reading about it.' — each a solitary negation, not a chained construction); no anaphora/epistrophe triple; no self-grading superlative; no number+own-retraction; no abstraction-noun stack (body stays concrete throughout — 'A fact. A role. A preference. A constraint.'); no verb triplet with an empty leg. The diff's repeated noun 'session' (lines 9, 11 x2, 19, plus a pre-existing unrelated use at line 25) matches none of the six listed shapes — it is plain vocabulary reuse of a mandated platform term (vocabulary.md line 11), not a cadence tic this rule names. PASS; the repetition question itself is logged in rule_questions since it falls outside this rule's enumerated patterns.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: repo/maintainer vocabulary projected on a wall is unparsable to the room. Checked body for dialect terms (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood-as-noun, Connections-as-proper-noun): none present. 'session' is not dialect: vocabulary.md line 11 names it explicit REQUIRED platform vocabulary ('the word on the student's screen... session, skill, subagent...'), the opposite of internal dialect — so the window→session diff is a move toward compliance with the platform-vocabulary law, not away from it. PASS.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: bold-as-claim-bullets swamps the slide with false handles. Ran grep -n '\*\*' curriculum/lectures/the-wizard-move.md, then filtered to body lines (<29): zero matches — no bold spans anywhere in the body. Consistent with the maintainer's own standing constraint at line 32 ('Zero bold on the narrative and demo slides'), and the diff touched no bold markup. PASS.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: content present in long-read but absent from the composed deck silently strands a reader who toggled to Slides. The diff touched only inline nouns inside three body sentences (lines 9, 11, 19) plus maintainer-block lines; no heading, phase wrapper, or section was added, removed, or moved. Ran node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/lectures/the-wizard-move.md → 'files: 1  slides: 4' — the checker still enumerates all 4 non-title ## sections for this file, matching the prior pin's structure exactly. Presence unaffected by this diff. PASS (structural claim carried from the efe8d58d pin; nothing in this diff could change deck inclusion).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: hand-numbered headers drift out of sync with the renderer's computed position. This file has no '## Phase N:' or '## N.' step headers (headings are 'Who this is for' / 'Context is King' / 'You steer the answer by loading context' / 'The loop is what you repeat' — none numbered). Ran node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js (full corpus) and grepped its output for 'wizard-move': no match, confirming no numbering issue flagged for this file. N/A + mechanically confirmed clean.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a positional pointer ('below', 'above', 'at the top') aims at a wall once the renderer cuts at ##. Ran node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/lectures/the-wizard-move.md → exact output: 'OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.' Mechanically confirmed clean; the diff introduced no positional language. PASS.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a label-shaped header on a lecture wastes the beat where a law should be named instead. No heading text changed in this diff. PASS, unaffected by the diff.
